summary:
### TL;DR
- **Allowlist update needed:** GitHub Actions on github.com is adding new blob storage hosts. If your network allowlist names individual hosts, add the new ones to keep job summaries and logs working. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-22-meta-api-endpoints-updated-for-actions-blob-storage))
- **Public monitoring for data residency:** Secret scanning public monitoring is now in public preview for GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (GHEC DR). It attributes exposed credentials using verified domain matching. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-22-public-monitoring-now-available-with-data-residency))
- **Copilot in Visual Studio:** You can now fix NuGet vulnerabilities from the Error List. There is also a breaking change to Bring Your Own Model (BYOM). ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-22-github-copilot-in-visual-studio-september-update-2))

### Action required
- **Actions blob storage allowlist (no deadline stated).** The meta API now lists these new hosts. Both ranges are inclusive. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-22-meta-api-endpoints-updated-for-actions-blob-storage))
  - `productionresultssa30.blob.core.windows.net` through `productionresultssa49.blob.core.windows.net`
  - `productionresultssa100.blob.core.windows.net` through `productionresultssa199.blob.core.windows.net`

  What to do:
  - If you already allow `productionresultssa*.blob.core.windows.net`, no change is needed.
  - If you allow individual hosts, add the new ones. Otherwise job summaries and logs may be interrupted.
  - You can get the current endpoint list from the REST API endpoints for meta data.
- **Visual Studio Copilot BYOM breaking change (affects Copilot users, not Actions).** ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-22-github-copilot-in-visual-studio-september-update-2))
  - BYOM now requires the new Agent (Preview), built on the GitHub Copilot SDK-powered harness.
  - The previous Ask and Agent modes no longer support BYOM.
  - You must re-add any Ollama models you configured before updating.

### Security improvements
- **Public monitoring for GHEC with data residency (public preview).** ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-22-public-monitoring-now-available-with-data-residency))
  - **What it does:** Secret scanning monitors public commits across github.com and attributes exposed credentials to your enterprise in real time.
  - **How attribution works:** In data residency regions, it relies only on verified domain matching. Enterprise membership rosters are not shared across the tenant-isolation boundary.
  - **How alerts are delivered:** Alerts are encrypted and delivered to your enterprise dashboard, and the data stays within your designated geography.
  - **Requirements:** An active GitHub Advanced Security or GitHub Secret Protection license. It is included at no additional cost.
  - **How to enable:** Enterprise admins or enterprise security managers can turn it on in enterprise security settings.
  - **Action for you:** Make sure your enterprise has verified its domains, since attribution depends on them.
- **NuGet vulnerability fixer in Visual Studio.** ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-22-github-copilot-in-visual-studio-september-update-2))
  - NuGet Audit warnings in the Error List now include a fixer action.
  - The fixer opens Copilot Chat in agent mode and asks Copilot to fix the vulnerable packages using the NuGet MCP server.
  - It requires signing in to Copilot and enabling the NuGet MCP server from the Copilot Chat tools menu.
  - It is available on all Copilot plans.

### Docs changes worth reading
Nothing this time.

changelog.title: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — September update
changelog.text: September 2026 brought deeper visibility into your work: explore pull requests without leaving chat, bring the AI model your team trusts, and fix vulnerable packages the moment Visual Studio flags them. Highlights Here’s what’s new with GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio 2026. Check the Insiders channel for the latest: Explore pull requests with the Git agent : The Git agent can now explore a pull request for you. Open GitHub Copilot Chat, select the Git agent, and attach a pull request as context from the Git Repository window to get a summary with navigable links to the underlying comments and files. This functionality requires connecting your Git provider’s MCP servers; GitHub and Azure DevOps are both supported. Updates to Bring Your Own Model (BYOM) : BYOM is available in preview and lets you use the models your team prefers, through GitHub Copilot or your own model deployments, whether or not you’re signed in to GitHub. This feature is on by default across the Community, Professional, and Enterprise editions. Breaking change: BYOM now requires the new Agent (Preview), built on the GitHub Copilot SDK-powered harness. The previous Ask and Agent modes no longer support BYOM, and you’ll need to re-add previously configured Ollama models after updating. Supported providers include Microsoft Foundry, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama. Fix NuGet Vulnerabilities from the Error List : NuGet Audit warnings in the Error List now include a fixer action that opens GitHub Copilot Chat in agent mode and asks Copilot to fix the vulnerable packages using the NuGet MCP server. This functionality requires signing in to GitHub Copilot and enabling the NuGet MCP server from the Copilot Chat tools menu. This update is available to users on all GitHub Copilot plans , including Copilot Free, Student, Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise. Download Visual Studio 2026 to experience all the new Copilot features today. To learn more about what’s new, check out the Visual Studio blog and release notes . What’s next for Copilot in Visual Studio Stay up to date on the latest Copilot features by following the Visual Studio blog , where you’ll find roadmap updates and opportunities to share feedback. The post GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — September update appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Meta API endpoints updated for Actions blob storage
changelog.text: We’re adding blob storage endpoints for GitHub Actions on github.com as part of our ongoing work to improve capacity and reliability. The meta API now includes these new endpoints. If your organization uses a network allowlist to access GitHub Actions blob storage, review your network access settings and ensure you allow the following new hosts (both ranges are inclusive): productionresultssa30.blob.core.windows.net through productionresultssa49.blob.core.windows.net productionresultssa100.blob.core.windows.net through productionresultssa199.blob.core.windows.net If you already allow productionresultssa*.blob.core.windows.net , no changes are needed for these additions. If you allow individual hosts, add the new hosts to avoid interruptions to job summaries and logs. For guidance on allowlisting GitHub traffic, see GitHub’s IP addresses . You can retrieve the current endpoint list using the REST API endpoints for meta data . The post Meta API endpoints updated for Actions blob storage appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Public monitoring now available with data residency
changelog.text: Public monitoring is now available in public preview for GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (GHEC DR). Public monitoring with data residency Public monitoring extends secret scanning beyond internal repositories by monitoring public commits across github.com, attributing exposed credentials back to your enterprise in real time. For enterprises hosted in data residency regions, attribution is powered exclusively by verified domain matching. Because data residency environments maintain strict tenant isolation from github.com, enterprise membership rosters are not shared across the boundary. Instead, when a commit author’s email matches a domain your enterprise has verified, the alert is encrypted and delivered directly to your enterprise dashboard while ensuring data stays within your designated geography. Eligibility and billing Public monitoring is available in public preview for GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers with data residency. Using public monitoring requires an active GitHub Advanced Security or GitHub Secret Protection license. Enterprise admins and enterprise security managers can enable the feature under enterprise security settings. Public monitoring is included with your GitHub Advanced Security or GitHub Secret Protection license at no additional cost. Learn more Learn more about secret scanning and verifying domains for your enterprise , or share your feedback in the community discussion . The post Public monitoring now available with data residency appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
